plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. Any bid below your value risks losing the auction to someone bidding slightly above your value, resulting in a missed opportunity to profit. Any bid above your value risks overpaying, reducing or eliminating profit. Since this is round 1 of 1, and my value is $40, I will bid my true value.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your value divided by 2. This is because if you bid higher than your value, you risk winning and losing money. If you bid significantly lower, you likely won't win, foregoing potential profit. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I will bid slightly below half my value to test the waters.

Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any deviation from your true value can be exploited by other rational bidders. If you bid below your value, you might lose the auction to someone who values the item more, even if their bid is only slightly above yours. If you bid above your value, you risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to you. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $17.
